name: Double uterus-hemivagina-renal agenesis syndrome
aliases: Obstructed hemivagina and ipsilateral renal anomaly (OHVIRA) syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and imaging diagnostic criteria for OHVIRA syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of uterus didelphys (double uterus) confirmed by imaging
Obstructed hemivagina demonstrated by clinical exam and imaging
Ipsilateral renal agenesis or dysplasia confirmed by ultrasound or MRI
Recurrent cyclical pelvic pain after menarche
Accumulation of menstrual blood in obstructed hemivagina

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of uterus didelphys with obstructed hemivagina and ipsilateral renal agenesis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on imaging studies including ultrasound and MRI combined with clinical findings.

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; possible mild leukocytosis if infection present
imaging: Ultrasound showing uterus didelphys and absent ipsilateral kidney
MRI pelvis confirming obstructed hemivagina and hematocolpos
Intravenous pyelogram or CT urography confirming renal agenesis
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; considered a congenital malformation
other: Physical examination revealing vaginal septum and pelvic mass

distinguishingFeatures: Single uterus with transverse vaginal septum rather than uterine duplication
Obstruction at hymenal level without renal anomalies
Single uterine horn with rudimentary horn, not uterus didelphys
May have renal anomalies but different uterine morphology

redFlags: Severe cyclical pelvic pain with palpable pelvic mass
Recurrent urinary tract infections with renal agenesis
references: Herlyn-Werner-Wunderlich syndrome: clinical and imaging features. Radiographics. 2010.
Congenital anomalies of the female reproductive tract: diagnosis and management. Obstet Gynecol Clin North Am. 2017.
